text.p: German engineering firm Deutsche Babcock AG on Friday said it "categorically rejected" rumours on the Frankfurt stock exchange that it was facing insolvency and said its restructing programme was progressing well.

A four-line regulatory news release gave no further details. But it follows a stock market pounding taken in recent weeks by the company after it said in mid-October it would take a larger than expected charge for restructuring measures.
Deutsche Babcock stock has been in a long, steep decline, closing on Thursday at a year-low of 45.20 marks, down from a high of 137 marks.

The company said on October 14 that it would take a larger than expected restructuring charge due to the closure of its Magdeburg plant and other key changes stemming from a business plan drawn up in July.

It also said that its core operating subsidiaries would meet their profit targets this year. Analysts doubt Babcock will meet its loss target of 400 million marks for the 1995/96 financial year to September 30.
